prompt: Explain why the sky is blue, briefly.
text:
Sunlight appears white but contains all colors of the rainbow. As it passes through Earth's atmosphere, gas molecules and tiny particles scatter the light. Blue light has shorter wavelengths and scatters much more strongly than red light, which has longer wavelengths. This phenomenon is called Rayleigh scattering.

Because blue light is scattered in all directions, when you look up at the sky, your eyes detect this scattered blue light coming from every part of the atmosphere. At sunset, sunlight travels through more atmosphere, scattering away most of the blue light and allowing the longer wavelengths (reds and oranges) to reach your eyes directly.
